question: While checking the wheels and rims on a pre-trip inspection, what does rust around the wheel nuts most likely signal?
choice_a: That the rim was recently repaired by welding
choice_b: That the nuts may be loose and their tightness should be checked
choice_c: That the tire is a mismatched size
choice_d: That the wheel bearings need to be repacked
explanation: The manual notes that rust around wheel nuts may mean the nuts are loose, and tells the driver to check tightness (and re-check after a tire change).
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-1

question: If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring, what does the manual say happens to the vehicle?
choice_a: It may still be driven if the load is light
choice_b: It must be reported but can be driven for 500 more miles
choice_c: It only affects ride comfort, not safety
choice_d: It will be put "out of service"
explanation: Under suspension system defects, the manual states missing or broken leaves in a leaf spring are dangerous, and if one-fourth or more are missing, the vehicle will be placed "out of service."
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-1

question: How much steering wheel play does the manual identify as enough to make a vehicle hard to steer?
choice_a: Any play greater than zero
choice_b: More than 30 degrees, about a quarter turn
choice_c: More than 90 degrees, a quarter turn of the wheel
choice_d: More than 10 degrees, about 2 inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel
explanation: The manual lists steering wheel play of more than 10 degrees (about 2 inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch steering wheel) as something that can make a vehicle hard to steer.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-1

question: Step 1 of the seven-step inspection method is "Vehicle Overview." What must be reviewed at this step, and what is the motor carrier obligated to do?
choice_a: The fuel receipts must be reviewed, and the carrier must reimburse the driver
choice_b: The last vehicle inspection report must be reviewed, and the carrier must repair any items in it that affect safety and certify the repairs
choice_c: The driver's medical card must be reviewed, and the carrier must renew it if expired
choice_d: The bill of lading must be reviewed, and the carrier must verify the cargo weight
explanation: Step 1 requires reviewing the last vehicle inspection report; the motor carrier must repair any items in the report affecting safety and certify that repairs were made or were unnecessary.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-2

question: After starting the engine, what does it mean if the ABS indicator light on the dash stays on instead of turning off?
choice_a: The transmission fluid is low
choice_b: The Anti-lock Braking System is not working properly
choice_c: The engine oil needs to be changed immediately
choice_d: The parking brake has failed
explanation: The manual states that the ABS dash light should come on and then turn off; if it stays on, the ABS is not working properly (and for trailers, a yellow light staying on at the left rear means the same).
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-3

question: According to the gauge checks after starting the engine, air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within what time frame, and to roughly what governor cut-out range?
choice_a: Within 10 minutes, building to a governor cut-out usually around 200 psi
choice_b: Within 3 minutes, building to a governor cut-out usually around 120-140 psi
choice_c: Within 1 minute, building to a governor cut-out usually around 100 psi
choice_d: Within 30 seconds, building to a governor cut-out usually around 80 psi
explanation: The manual states air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes, continuing to a governor cut-out usually around 120-140 psi.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-3

question: On a manual-transmission vehicle, what should a driver do to keep from rolling back when starting from a stop?
choice_a: Shift into a higher gear before releasing the brake
choice_b: Partly engage the clutch before taking the right foot off the brake
choice_c: Release the clutch fully before touching the accelerator
choice_d: Rev the engine to full throttle before releasing the brake
explanation: The manual advises partly engaging the clutch before taking the right foot off the brake, and applying the parking brake if needed to avoid rolling back.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-7

question: If the drive wheels begin to spin while accelerating on poor traction, what does the manual say to do?
choice_a: Take your foot off the accelerator
choice_b: Shift into neutral immediately
choice_c: Press the accelerator down further to power through it
choice_d: Apply the parking brake
explanation: The manual warns that using too much power on poor traction can spin the drive wheels and cause loss of control, and instructs the driver to take their foot off the accelerator if the wheels begin to spin.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-7

question: How does the manual say a driver should hold the steering wheel?
choice_a: With one hand while the other rests on the console
choice_b: Loosely, so it can self-correct after hitting bumps
choice_c: With both hands close together at the top of the wheel
choice_d: Firmly, with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel
explanation: The manual instructs holding the wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides, so it does not get pulled from the driver's hands after hitting a curb or pothole.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-7

question: What braking technique does the manual recommend for a smooth, safe stop?
choice_a: Rely on the parking brake instead of the foot brake
choice_b: Push the brake pedal down gradually and control the pressure
choice_c: Push the brake pedal down as hard as possible right away
choice_d: Pump the brake pedal rapidly at every stop
explanation: The manual says to push the brake pedal down gradually and control the pressure so the vehicle comes to a smooth, safe stop, pushing the clutch in as the engine nears idle on a manual transmission.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-7

question: Why does the manual recommend backing and turning toward the driver's side whenever possible, even if it means going around the block?
choice_a: Because it is required by state law in every situation
choice_b: Because it lets the driver watch the rear of the vehicle through the side window, unlike backing toward the right
choice_c: Because it reduces wear on the right-side tires
choice_d: Because it keeps the exhaust from blowing toward pedestrians
explanation: The manual explains that backing toward the driver's side lets the driver watch the rear of the vehicle out the side window, while backing toward the right side is very dangerous because visibility is worse.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-8

question: Per the manual, which type of manual transmission requires double clutching, and which does not?
choice_a: Unsynchronized manual transmissions require it; double clutching is NOT required on a synchronized manual transmission
choice_b: Neither type requires double clutching on heavy vehicles
choice_c: Synchronized manual transmissions require it; unsynchronized transmissions never need it
choice_d: Both types always require double clutching
explanation: The manual states most heavy vehicles with unsynchronized manual transmissions require double clutching to change gears, while double clutching is NOT required on a synchronized manual transmission.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-8

question: Why does the manual say a driver should slow down and downshift before starting down a hill?
choice_a: So the engine can be shut off to save fuel while coasting
choice_b: So the driver can safely release the steering wheel briefly
choice_c: So the transmission can be shifted into neutral for the entire descent
choice_d: So the vehicle can be controlled without using the brakes hard, since overheated brakes can lose their braking power
explanation: The manual explains that downshifting before a hill lets the driver control speed without using the brakes hard, since overheating the brakes can cause them to lose their braking power.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-8

question: What benefit does the manual give for downshifting to the right gear before entering a curve, rather than after?
choice_a: It allows the driver to skip using the steering wheel through the curve
choice_b: It prevents the transmission from overheating in hot weather
choice_c: It lets the driver use some power through the curve, which helps the vehicle stay stable and speed up once out of the curve
choice_d: It is only useful for automatic transmissions, not manual ones
explanation: The manual states that downshifting before entering a curve lets the driver use some power through the curve to help the vehicle stay more stable, and allows speeding up once out of the curve.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-9

question: The manual lists four basic types of retarders. When should a retarder be turned off?
choice_a: Only when the vehicle is empty
choice_b: Only above 55 mph
choice_c: Whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered, because it may cause the drive wheels to skid
choice_d: Retarders should never be turned off once engaged
explanation: The manual describes four basic types of retarders (exhaust, engine, hydraulic, electric) and cautions that when drive wheels have poor traction, the retarder may cause them to skid, so it should be turned off on wet, icy, or snow-covered roads.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-9

question: The manual says most good drivers look how far ahead of their vehicle while driving?
choice_a: About 2 to 3 seconds ahead
choice_b: At least 12 to 15 seconds ahead
choice_c: At least one full minute ahead
choice_d: Only as far as the headlights reach at night
explanation: The manual states most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead, which is about one block at lower speeds or about a quarter mile at highway speeds.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-9

question: When can mirror adjustment be checked accurately on a combination vehicle, according to the manual?
choice_a: Only at night with headlights on
choice_b: Only when the trailer(s) are straight
choice_c: Only after the engine has warmed up for 15 minutes
choice_d: Only while backing up
explanation: The manual states mirror adjustment should be checked prior to the start of any trip and can only be checked accurately when the trailer(s) are straight.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-10

question: How do curved (convex) mirrors change the way objects appear, according to the manual?
choice_a: Objects appear at exactly the same size and distance as in a flat mirror
choice_b: Objects appear larger and closer than they really are
choice_c: Objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are
choice_d: Objects appear upside down
explanation: The manual explains that everything appears smaller in a convex mirror than it would look directly, and things also seem farther away than they really are, so drivers must allow for this.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-10

question: During a lane change, what should a driver check for right after signaling, according to the manual's mirror-check sequence?
choice_a: That the fuel gauge shows enough fuel to complete the lane change
choice_b: That the trailer brake hand valve is released
choice_c: That no one has moved into the driver's blind spot
choice_d: That the four-way flashers are off
explanation: The manual's lane-change mirror checks include checking mirrors after signaling to make sure no one has moved into the driver's blind spot, in addition to checks before, during, and after the lane change.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-10

question: The manual gives three rules for using turn signals. What are they?
choice_a: Signal after beginning the turn, signal intermittently, and cancel before turning
choice_b: Signal early, signal continuously, and cancel the signal after completing the turn
choice_c: Signal only when traffic is heavy, signal briefly, and leave the signal on afterward
choice_d: Signal only for left turns, signal loudly with the horn, and cancel immediately
explanation: The manual's three rules for turn signals are: signal early, signal continuously (don't cancel until the turn is complete), and cancel the signal after turning.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-11

question: When it is legal, what does the manual suggest doing before passing a pedestrian or bicyclist who may not see you?
choice_a: Honk the horn continuously until you have fully passed
choice_b: Turn on the four-way emergency flashers and keep them on through the pass
choice_c: Tap the horn lightly, or at night flash your lights from low to high beam and back
choice_d: Swerve wide into the next lane without any warning
explanation: The manual advises tapping the horn lightly, or at night flashing lights from low to high beam and back, when passing someone who may not see you, while still driving carefully in case they don't respond.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-11

question: If you must stop on or by a one-way or divided highway, at what distances should you place your warning devices toward the approaching traffic?
choice_a: 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet
choice_b: 5 feet, 50 feet, and 100 feet
choice_c: 20 feet, 150 feet, and 300 feet
choice_d: 50 feet, 250 feet, and 500 feet
explanation: The manual states that on a one-way or divided highway, warning devices should be placed 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward the approaching traffic.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-11

question: If you stop on a two-lane road carrying traffic in both directions, where should you place your warning devices?
choice_a: Only 500 feet behind the vehicle
choice_b: Within 10 feet of the front or rear corners of the vehicle, and 100 feet behind and ahead of it
choice_c: 300 feet behind and 300 feet ahead of the vehicle
choice_d: Within 2 feet of the vehicle only, no farther out
explanation: The manual states that on a two-lane road carrying traffic in both directions, warning devices go within 10 feet of the front or rear corners to mark the vehicle's location, plus 100 feet behind and ahead of it.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-12

question: What is the average driver's reaction time before physically hitting the brakes after seeing a hazard, and how far does that account for at 55 mph?
choice_a: About 5 seconds, accounting for 400 feet traveled
choice_b: About 1/10 second, accounting for 8 feet traveled
choice_c: About 3 seconds, accounting for 240 feet traveled
choice_d: About 1/2 second to 1 second, accounting for 61 feet traveled
explanation: The manual states the average driver has a reaction time of 1/2 second to 1 second, which at 55 mph accounts for 61 feet of travel before the brakes are physically applied.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-13

question: What is the average perception time for an alert driver, and how far does that account for at 55 mph, per the manual?
choice_a: About 1/4 second, accounting for 20 feet traveled
choice_b: About 4 seconds, accounting for 320 feet traveled
choice_c: About 1-3/4 seconds, accounting for 142 feet traveled
choice_d: About 6 seconds, accounting for 500 feet traveled
explanation: The manual states the average perception time for an alert driver is 1-3/4 seconds, which at 55 mph accounts for 142 feet of travel before the driver even reacts.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-14

question: If you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, how does the manual say the impact and braking distance change?
choice_a: Both become 2 times greater
choice_b: Both become 4 times greater
choice_c: Both become 8 times greater
choice_d: Only the braking distance doubles; impact stays the same
explanation: The manual states that doubling speed from 20 to 40 mph makes the impact 4 times greater, and the braking distance is also 4 times longer.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-13

question: On a wet road, the manual's example says a driver should reduce speed by about how much?
choice_a: No reduction is needed as long as tires are new
choice_b: About one-third (for example, slowing from 55 to about 35 mph)
choice_c: About three-quarters (for example, slowing from 55 to about 14 mph)
choice_d: About one-tenth (for example, slowing from 55 to about 50 mph)
explanation: The manual instructs reducing speed by about one-third on a wet road, using the example of slowing from 55 to about 35 mph (with even greater reductions for packed snow or ice).
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-14

question: How slow does the manual say a vehicle can be going and still hydroplane, if there is a lot of water on the road?
choice_a: As low as 30 mph
choice_b: Speed is irrelevant to hydroplaning
choice_c: Hydroplaning requires at least 75 mph
choice_d: Only above 65 mph
explanation: The manual states hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is a lot of water on the road, and is more likely with low tire pressure or worn tread.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-14

question: What rule of thumb does the manual give for how much following distance to keep ahead of your vehicle at speeds below 40 mph?
choice_a: At least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length
choice_b: One second for each 50 feet of vehicle length
choice_c: Two car lengths for every 10 mph of speed
choice_d: A flat 3 seconds regardless of vehicle length
explanation: The manual's rule is at least one second of following distance for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph, adding 1 more second at speeds above 40 mph.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-15

question: If you notice you're being tailgated, what two things does the manual specifically advise against doing?
choice_a: Making quick changes in speed or direction, and speeding up
choice_b: Using your mirrors and slowing down gradually
choice_c: Turning on your headlights and braking smoothly
choice_d: Increasing your following distance and signaling early
explanation: The manual advises drivers who are tailgated to avoid quick changes in speed or direction and not to speed up, since it's safer to be tailgated at a low speed than a high one; increasing following distance is instead recommended.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-16
